The petitioners have filed this petition U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act,1988 claiming compensation amount from respondents due to death of husband of Petitioner No.1 in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief case of the petitioners is that, on 11-01-2023 at about 9.53a.m. the deceased Kumbara Hunurappa was crossing the Balagere Main Road from South to North direction on Balagere Main Road, at that time, the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-13/U-1929 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner at high speed from Varthur Police Station towards Balagere and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to forced impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately, after the accident, the rider of the Motorcycle hired the autorickshaw and the deceased was shifted to Vydehi Hospital, wherein the duty doctors were treated and declared he was died on the way to hospital.
After the postmortem, the body was handed over to the petitioners and they performed funeral, obsequies, last rites for which they have spent more than Rs.3,50,000/-.
4. Prior to the date of accident deceased was hale, healthy and aged about 46 years and working as mason/coolie and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

He was the only earning member in the family Kumbara Mangalamma vs Vigneshwaran.R on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13836402/
2 and he worked very hard to look after his family and had a bright future in his career.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and she has lost her husband's love and affection, caring at early age due to the fatal accident and he loved his wife and took great care about her and he had the burden of the entire family in his shoulders.
Petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of the deceased and he loved his children very much and now they have to grow without love and affection and guidelines of the father.
The petitioners were entirely depending upon the deceased.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the family members are completely broken and life has become desolated by the grief causing lot of pain, shock, mental agony and financial difficulties.
The petitioners were very much fond of and in love with the deceased.

5. The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN- 13/U-1929, against whom the Whitefield Traffic police filed criminal case in Cr.No.05/2023 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
6. The Respondent No.1 is being RC owner and respondent No.2 is being Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners pray to grant the compensation.
7. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statements.
8. The respondent No.1 has contended in his written statement that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

The averments of the claim petition are totally denied as false and the said accident took place because of the fault of the deceased only as he was blindly crossing the road without following traffic rules and regulations, because of the careless and reckless behaviour and attitude of the deceased the accident took place.

The deceased was drunk at the time of accident, all of a sudden crossed the road without observing traffic rules and regulations and hence, the accident took place in the middle of the road, it is not a place for pedestrian to cross or to walk, whee there is no zebra crossing nor a signal and this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

This respondent has further contended that he has insured the offending vehicle with the respondent No.2 and the said policy was in force as on the date of accident and he had a valid driving licence on the date of accident.

Further he has admitted that, he arranged the Autorickshaw for the injured and took him to hospital and paid the amount and further denied the accident took place because of this respondent who was riding his two wheeler.
The respondent No.1 has contended that the deceased was aged about 60 years on the date of accident.
9. Further denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased and denied the relationship of deceased with the petitioner.
It is contended that, the compensation amount claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
10. The respondent No.2 has contended in it's written statement that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

While admitting about issuance of insurance Kumbara Mangalamma vs Vigneshwaran.R on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13836402/
3 policy in respect of Two Wheeler and responsibility in terms and conditions, exceptions, limits and endorsement of the policy.

The respondent No.1 has been violated the mandatory provisions of the MV Act and he had been willfully and knowing fully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

The petitioners have filed a false case against the aforesaid vehicle to cause wrongful loss to this respondent, the earliest police records do not disclose the vehicle number which caused the accident.

Further, denied the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and denied the relationship of deceased with the petitioner.
It is contended that, the compensation amount claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

11. Based on the above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that, on 11-01- 2023 at about 9.53 a.m. when the deceased Kumbara Honnurappa was crossing the Balagere Main Road from South to North Direction, at that time, rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-13/U- 1929 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life, came from Varthur Police Station towards Balagere and dashed to the deceased.

As a result of forced impact,
the petitioner fell down on the road and died on the way to the hospital?
2) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much?

From whom?
3) Whether order or award?
12. In order to prove the case, petitioner No.2 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
Per contra, Respondent No.2 got examined its Assistant Manager as RW.1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and 2.
Ex.R.3 is marked on consent.
13. Heard the arguments on the side of the petitioner and respondent No.2.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has filed written arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

14. By considering the evidence and arguments, this court answer the following issues as under :
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

As per final order for the following:
REASONS 15. Issue No.1 :- The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for claiming compensation from the Respondents, due to death of husband of Petitioner No.1 and father of Kumbara Mangalamma vs Vigneshwaran.R on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13836402/

16.

In order to substantiate the case, the Petitioner No.2 got examined himself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and in his chief affidavit, he had reiterated the entire contention of petition and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.

17 . Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R, Ex.P.2 is the copy of Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of Spot Mahazar,

18. The Assistant Manager of the respondent No.2 got examined as RW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination, he had reiterated the contents of Written Statement and got marked 02 documents marked as Ex.R.1 is the authorization letter, Ex.R.2 is the certified copy of Insurance Policy.

19. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the deceased was crossing the Balagere Main Road from South to North direction, the accident took place due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was died on the way to the hospital, he was earning of Rs.30,000/- p.m. and he was aged about 46 years at the time of accident.
Petitioner No.1 to 4 are wholly dependents of the deceased.
Hence, prayed to award compensation as claimed.
20. PW1 in his cross-examination has stated that, he has not witnessed the accident, but denied that his father was drunk and crossing the road negligently.

Counsel for the respondent No.1 filed his written argument contending that, this Accident took place because of the fault of the deceased only as he was blindly crossing the road without following traffic rules and regulations and the said accident had occurred in the middle of the road.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the petition.
22. RW.1 has deposed that, the vehicle is not involved in the accident, it has been falsely implicated in the accident.
On perusal of the written statement of respondent No.1 it appears that, he has not denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
He has contended that after accident he booked an Autorickshaw and shifted the deceased to the hospital.
The bank statement of respondent No.1 is marked as Ex.R.3.
On perusal of Ex.R.3, it appears that on 11-01-2023 the UPI payment of Rs.200/- has been made.
The respondent No.1 in his written statement has also admitted that, he arranged Autorickshaw for the injured to took him to the hospital.

Therefore, it appears that this accident is caused by the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-13/U-1929.
23.
On perusal of Ex.P.6 IMV report, it discloses that, fresh damages are noticed on the motorcycle at the time of inspection.

On perusal of Ex.P.4 the sketch, it appears that the accident had occurred Kumbara Mangalamma vs Vigneshwaran.R on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13836402/
5 at the right portion of the road i.e., ahead in the middle portion of the road.
The deceased was crossed the road almost more than half.
The motorcycle came from its left side towards the right.
There was enough space on left side of the road to avoid the accident by the rider of offending vehicle.

On perusal of Spot sketch & Charge sheet which disclose that, when the deceased was crossing the road, the rider of the offending vehicle, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Hence, the Whitefield Traffic Police have filed Charge sheet against rider of offending vehicle as accused for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Therefore, it is clear that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
24. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioners have to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

25. The respondent No.2 has taken contention that the respondent No.1 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.2 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.2 has not proved that respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

26. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R, Ex.P.2- Complaint, Ex.P.3-Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4-Spot Sketch, Ex.P.5-Inquest Report, Ex.P.6-IMV Report, Ex.P.7-PM Report, Ex.P.8-Police Intimation and Ex.P.9-Charge sheet
, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-13/U-1929.
Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
27. Issue No.2: The petitioners claimed compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to death of husband of Petitioner No.1 Smt. Kumbara Mangalamma in a road traffic accident.
28. As per Ex.P.10 Notarized Copy of Aadhaar Card, date of birth of the deceased is shown as 01-01-1977.
As per Ex.P.5 Inquest Report and Ex.P.7 PM Report also age of the deceased is shown as 46 years.
On the basis of the date of birth of the deceased in the Aadhar Card, he was of 46 years old.
Hence, the age of the deceased is taken in between 46 to 50 at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier is 13.
29.
The petitioners not produced any document to prove the income and avocation of the deceased.
In present days a Coolie worker can get Rs.500/- to 600/- per day.

However the petitioners asserted that the deceased was working as mason/coolie and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m. though documents are not produced but, by considering the age, income and occupation of deceased this Tribunal took the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/-.
Kumbara Mangalamma vs Vigneshwaran.R on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13836402/
6 30.

With regard to the loss of future prospectus is concern, the Apex court in the earlier Judgment reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 (Rajesh & Ors Vs Rajbir Singh & Ors) also taken note of the fact that, self employed persons are also entitled for future prospectus and the said Judgment was referred to larger bench and the Apex court in the recent Judgment passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others.)

entities.text: 2013 ACJ 1403 (Rajesh & Ors Vs Rajbir Singh & Ors)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component"

Herein this case, the deceased was aged about 46 years & working as mason/coolie,
hence the Petitioners are entitled to claim 25% of future prospectus as per above citation, due to death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.
31. The petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased.
Hence, the Petitioners are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.

So, relying upon the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Varma and others - Vs- Delhi Transport Corporation & another), out of the salary of the deceased 1/4th has to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Varma and others - Vs- Delhi Transport Corporation & another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
a) Income of the deceased is taken Rs.16,000-00 at b) Addition of 25% income towards future prospectus:
Rs.20,000-00 Rs.16,000/- + 4,000/- (25%) =
c) Deduction towards personal expenses:
Rs.15,000-00 Rs.20,000/- - Rs.5,000/- (1/4th ) Therefore this tribunal took the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-, which comes as Rs.15,000/- X 12 X 13 = Rs.23,40,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,40,000/- under the head loss of dependency.
32. The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, she lost her husband at age of 42 years.

Regarding consortium, this tribunal has relied upon the decision of Rajesh and Others Vs. Rajbir Singh and Others reported in 2013 ACJ 1403, in which it is held as,
"Words and phrases - Consortium - Consortium is the right of spouse to the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, society, solace,
affection and sexual relations with his or her mate".

entities.text: Rajesh and Others Vs. Rajbir Singh and Others reported in 2013 ACJ 1403
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is not possible to compensate the loss of love and affection of the deceased with the Petitioner No.1 by compensating in quantum of amount.

In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court Kumbara Mangalamma vs Vigneshwaran.R on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13836402/
7 of India passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others) held that, Reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.

Therefore, in view of the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and by considering the loss of love, affection and care from her husband, this Tribunal awarded the reasonable compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
33. The Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased, they lost love, affection and future support of the deceased.

In this regard the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Magma General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors., (Civil Appeal No.9581/2018 (Arising out of SLP (civil) 3192/2018) was held that:
The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors., (Civil Appeal No.9581/2018 (Arising out of
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
A few High courts have awarded compensation on this count.
However, there was no clarity with respect to the principles on which compensation could be awarded on loss of Filial Consortium.

The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium"
as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).
In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000/- each, for loss of Filial Consortium.
Hence, the Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation amount at Rs.40,000/-each under the head loss of Filial Consortium.

34. Towards awarding compensation under the head of transportation of dead body, funeral &
obsequies ceremonies, the Petitioners have not produced any documents.

However by considering the expenses towards funeral & obsequies ceremonies of deceased and in view of judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others) it is just and proper to award a Rs.15,000/- under the head of transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremonies.

8 35.

Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads of: Amount in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 23,40,000/-
 2. Loss of consortium 40,000/-
 3. Towards loss of Filial 1,20,000/-
 Consortium.
 4. Towards funeral and 15,000/-
 obsequies ceremonies

5 . Towards loss of estate 15,000/-
 Total 25,30,000/-
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,30,000/-.
36. Interest:

For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
37. Liability:-
As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-13/U-1929.
As already discussed in the issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the Respondent No.1 and 2 being RC Owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Further the Respondent No.2 is being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
38. Issue No.3:-

For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the Petitioners is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,30,000/- with interest @

9 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount.
Further, respondent No.2 shall indemnify the respondent No.1 and shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.16,30,000/- with interest.
The Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.3,00,000/-each with interest.

After deposit, 50% of the compensation amount allotted to the share of petitioner No.1 shall be released in favour of the petitioner No.1 with proper identification and the remaining share amount shall be deposited in FD in the name of Petitioner No.1,
in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.

After deposit, Rs.2,00,000/-each shall be with proper identification and the remaining share amount shall be deposited in FD in the name of Petitioner No.2 to 4, in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

The petitioners have filed this petition U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act,1988 claiming compensation amount from respondents due to death of husband of Petitioner No.1 in a road traffic accident.
The deceased was drunk at the time of accident, all of a sudden crossed the road without observing traffic rules and regulations and hence, the accident took place in the middle of the road, it is not a place for pedestrian to cross or to walk, whee there is no zebra crossing nor a signal and this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.arguments: The respondent No.1 has been violated the mandatory provisions of the MV Act and he had been willfully and knowing fully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
11. Based on the above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that, on 11-01- 2023 at about 9.53 a.m. when the deceased Kumbara Honnurappa was crossing the Balagere Main Road from South to North Direction, at that time, rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-13/U- 1929 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life, came from Varthur Police Station towards Balagere and dashed to the deceased.
As a result of forced impact,
the petitioner fell down on the road and died on the way to the hospital?
2) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much?
From whom?
3) Whether order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The deceased was crossed the road almost more than half.
There was enough space on left side of the road to avoid the accident by the rider of offending vehicle.
On perusal of Spot sketch & Charge sheet which disclose that, when the deceased was crossing the road, the rider of the offending vehicle, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Hence, the Whitefield Traffic Police have filed Charge sheet against rider of offending vehicle as accused for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Therefore, it is clear that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
24. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.2 has not proved that respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, the Petitioners are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.
Hence, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,40,000/- under the head loss of dependency.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium"
as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).
For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-13/U-1929.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000/- each, for loss of Filial Consortium.
Hence, the Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation amount at Rs.40,000/-each under the head loss of Filial Consortium.
Further the petitioners are also entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head loss of estate.
5 . Towards loss of estate 15,000/-
 Total 25,30,000/-
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,30,000/-.
37. Liability:-
Hence, the Respondent No.1 and 2 being RC Owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Further the Respondent No.2 is being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
38. Issue No.3:-
For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the Petitioners is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,30,000/- with interest @

9 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount.
Further, respondent No.2 shall indemnify the respondent No.1 and shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.16,30,000/- with interest.
The Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.3,00,000/-each with interest.

in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.
After deposit, Rs.2,00,000/-each shall be with proper identification and the remaining share amount shall be deposited in FD in the name of Petitioner No.2 to 4, in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
